Cross-Validated Discrete-Time KL Model with an Elastic-Net Penalty

cv.discretekl_enet.Rd

Chooses the integration weight eta and the lasso / elastic-net penalty lambda of discretekl_enet() together, by K-fold cross-validation of the pooled held-out negative log-likelihood. It is the discrete-time counterpart of cv.coxkl_enet().

Usage

cv.discretekl_enet(
  z,
  delta,
  interval,
  stratum = NULL,
  hazard = NULL,
  beta = NULL,
  baseline = NULL,
  etas,
  alpha = 1,
  lambda = NULL,
  nlambda = 100,
  lambda.min.ratio = NULL,
  link = c("cloglog", "logit"),
  n_intervals = NULL,
  nfolds = 5,
  seed = NULL,
  standardize = TRUE,
  tol = 1e-09,
  Mstop = 200,
  message = FALSE
)

Arguments

z

Numeric matrix (or data frame of numeric columns) of covariates, one row per subject. Column names are used to align external coefficients by name.

delta

Event indicator: 1 when the event happened in the subject's last interval at risk, 0 when the subject was censored at the end of it.

interval

Whole numbers \(1, \dots, K\): the last interval each subject was at risk in (the interval of the event when delta = 1).

stratum

Optional strata; each stratum has its own baseline hazard over the intervals.

hazard

Optional \(n \times K\) matrix of external interval hazards: row \(i\), column \(k\) is the external model's probability that subject \(i\) has the event in interval \(k\) given that it reached the interval. If not supplied, beta and baseline must be.

beta

Optional named vector of external Cox coefficients, aligned to colnames(z) by name (covariates the external model does not cover are set to 0; see align_beta()).

baseline

Optional external baseline cumulative-hazard increments over intervals \(1, \dots, K\), \(\Delta\Lambda_0(k) = \Lambda_0(t_k) - \Lambda_0(t_{k-1})\). With beta, the external interval hazard is \(1 - \exp\{-e^{z^\top\beta}\Delta\Lambda_0(k)\}\).

etas

Numeric vector of non-negative candidate weights (required). Include 0 to compare with the target model alone.

alpha

Elastic-net mixing parameter in \((0, 1]\); alpha = 1 (the default) is the lasso.

lambda

Optional penalty values used for every eta; NULL builds a path for each eta.

nlambda

Number of penalty values when lambda is NULL. Default 100.

lambda.min.ratio

Smallest penalty as a fraction of the largest; NULL uses 0.05 when there are more covariates than subjects and 1e-3 otherwise (a tenth of that for the ridge).

link

"cloglog" (complementary log-log: the grouped proportional-hazards model, the default, on the scale of a Cox model's coefficients) or "logit" (proportional odds of the interval hazard).

n_intervals

Number of intervals \(K\); defaults to max(interval).

nfolds

Number of folds. Default 5.

seed

Optional integer seed of the fold assignment. Folds are assigned at random within the events and within the censored subjects (within strata when stratum is given), so the same seed gives the same folds to every model fitted on the same data.

standardize

Standardize the covariates before penalizing; coefficients are returned on the original scale. Default TRUE.

tol

Convergence tolerance of the Fisher-scoring iterations. Default 1e-9.

Mstop

Maximum number of iterations per fit. Default 200.

message

Logical; if TRUE, prints a progress bar.

Value

An object of class "cv.discretekl_enet": as cv.discretekl_ridge(), plus alpha.

See also

discretekl_enet(), cv.discretekl_ridge()

Examples

data(ExampleData_discrete)
tr <- ExampleData_discrete$train
cvfit <- cv.discretekl_enet(z = tr$z, delta = tr$status, interval = tr$interval,
                            beta = ExampleData_discrete$beta_external,
                            baseline = ExampleData_discrete$baseline_external,
                            etas = c(0, 1, 10), nlambda = 10, seed = 1)
#> 1 covariate(s) absent from external 'beta' were set to 0: Z6.
cvfit$best$best_beta
#>         Z1         Z2         Z3         Z4         Z5         Z6 
#>  0.6430738 -0.5629570  0.6833370 -0.6367590  0.2919311 -0.0527131
